## Source: amazon-inspector (b99ca6a65bd9e71ec0333a05a272ad0b11773ca20630f9d02ad79345a64b8fdc)
The package presents itself as a utility library but exports nothing (index.js is 188 bytes and only require()s a platform-specific native addon). Three precompiled native binaries are shipped (native_win.node, native_mac.node, native.napi.node) alongside a 1,192,296-byte opaque `.napi_cache` blob with zero printable strings and no native source. Strings in the binaries show the addon reads `.napi_cache`, writes a staged JS file matching `%s.nc%lu.js` (Linux/mac also `/tmp/.%u`), and executes it via `node "%s"` using `CreateProcessA` on Windows and `fork`/`execlp` on Linux/mac. The loader is gated on CI environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD) and includes anti-analysis checks (CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, process enumeration via Process32First, strings referencing `wireshark` and `httpdebug`, container/daemon detection via `/proc/1/cgroup` and `dockerinit`, `setsid` + `__IS_DAEMON`). Any `require()` of this package on a matching CI host decrypts and executes attacker-controlled code from the shipped blob under the installer's build identity. The package metadata is a thin stub (random-looking name, no author, no repository, description `utility library`) consistent with a disposable build-system targeting dropper rather than a real library.
